1.title: Find the right sites for chargers
1.intro: Chargers earn where cars stop for a while and power is available.
pts: Types: home, workplace, destination (1-4 hours), fast (20-40 minutes).
Site scores: dwell time, traffic, nearby amenities, grid power, safety, cost to connect.
Visit three sites; count cars parked per hour.
Write a one-page site pitch to an owner.
1.ex: Shopping centre: average stay 90 minutes, 60 EV cars a day, grid connection 150 kW available; score 4.2/5.
1.act: Score three sites and choose one.

2.title: Know electrical and utility rules
2.intro: Charging involves electricity and public safety.
pts: Electrical work follows the provincial code and licensed electricians; permits and inspections are required.
Utility connection agreements set capacity and timing.
Accessibility and signage rules apply.
Selling electricity by the kWh is regulated by province; check how to charge.
2.ex: Row: 'Install a fast charger | provincial electrical authority | permit and inspection | before energising | inspection certificate'.
2.act: Build a rules table for one site.

3.title: Plan the installation
pts: Compute power: number of chargers x kW, with load management to share capacity.
Plan cables, trenching, lighting and drainage.
Choose connectors and payment methods that suit local cars.
Plan remote monitoring.
3.ex: 4 chargers of 50 kW on a 150 kW supply with load sharing: no more than 3 run at full power at once.
3.act: Draw a site layout and load plan.

4.title: Price charging and prove the business
4.intro: Revenue per kWh, minus power cost and fees.
pts: Energy margin = selling price - energy price - network fees.
Add idle fees to free the bay.
Include maintenance, software and site lease.
Compute payback.
4.ex: Charger 18,000 installed 11,000... usage 12 sessions a day x 28 kWh x margin 0.18 per kWh = 60 a day. Teaching figures in CAD.
4.act: Build a payback model with a low-use case.

5.title: Operate reliably
pts: Monitor remotely; alert on faults.
Respond within a set time.
Clean and inspect monthly.
Track uptime and sessions.
5.ex: Uptime 97% target; fault repaired within 24 hours.

6.title: Win site hosts and drivers
pts: Offer revenue share to site owners.
List on charging maps.
Offer fleet plans.
Collect feedback.

7.title: Manage safety and grid risk
7.intro: Plan for hazards and demand peaks.
pts: Cable and trip hazards, vandalism, weather.
Peak demand charges.
Cyber security for chargers.
Insurance.
7.ex: Risk: 'Peak demand charge | 3 x 4 | load management | ops | monthly'.

8.title: Pilot and expand
pts: 90 days.
Measure sessions, kWh, uptime.
Stop rule: under 3 sessions a day after 60 days means move or adjust price.
Plan roll-out.

quiz: How long a car stays parked.
Who may do the electrical work?
Licensed electricians with permits and inspection.
Selling price minus energy price and fees.
To free the bay for others.
About 97% or better, with repair inside 24 hours.
A fee based on peak power drawn.
Under 3 sessions a day after 60 days.
